chief_complaint: desire for highly effective long-term birth control
hpi_details: A 27-year-old female presents to discuss highly effective long-term contraception.
concerns: She is worried that an implant or coil will cause severe weight gain, bad skin breakouts, or long-term damage to her fertility.
expectations: She hopes to compare the arm implant and intrauterine device side-by-side and find out if she can have one inserted today.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Contraceptive counseling for long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Contraceptive counseling for long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Contraceptive Counseling LARC: Discuss IUD (Mirena/Copper) vs Nexplanon implant, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Contraceptive counseling for long-acting reversible contraception (LARC).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Assuming counseling is unnecessary because the patient has no acute symptoms.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Screen for contraindications to hormonal methods (e.g., migraine with aura, clotting disorders).
management_principles: Plan for Contraceptive Counseling LARC: Discuss IUD (Mirena/Copper) vs Nexplanon implant
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: What methods of birth control have you used before, and what did you like or dislike?
Are you hoping to have children in the future, and if so, when?
Do you have migraines with aura, blood clotting problems, or smoke?
We can discuss a hormonal or copper IUD, or the Nexplanon arm implant; each lasts several years.

history.answer: I'm here today because I'd like to get counseling about a reliable, long-term birth control method.
I was hoping to compare the pros and cons of the arm implant versus the coil and see if I can get one placed today.
No, I feel completely healthy and have no physical complaints or pain today.
We have been using condoms recently, and in the past I tried oral contraceptive pills for about six months.
I often forgot to take the pill at the same time each day due to my busy schedule, which caused a lot of anxiety.
I definitely do not want to become pregnant for at least the next four to five years while I focus on my career.
I read a little about the arm implant and intrauterine devices like the hormonal or copper IUD, but I don't know which would suit me best.
I've read horror stories online about massive weight gain, and I'm scared that putting a device inside me could hurt my fertility later.
No, I haven't had any abnormal bleeding, spotting between my periods, or bleeding after intercourse.
My last menstrual period started exactly two weeks ago. My cycles are regular, arriving every twenty-eight days and lasting five days.
I don't think there is any chance I'm pregnant since we used condoms consistently, but I'm very willing to take a pregnancy test today.
I have been in a monogamous relationship with my partner for one year. We use condoms, and neither of us has ever had a sexually transmitted infection.
No, I rarely get headaches and have never had migraines, visual changes, or blind spots.
No, I have never had a blood clot in my legs or lungs, and no one in my immediate family has either.
My blood pressure has always been normal whenever it was checked at routine visits.
No, I have never had any breast masses, cysts, or a diagnosis of breast cancer.
I had a comprehensive checkup with a Pap smear last year, and everything was completely normal.
